answer:
We are here today to remember my brother, Jason Wilson, and to honor the life he lived and the place he holds in each of our hearts.

Jason passed away last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center, at the age of 67. It is hard to take in that he is gone. There is no single thing I can say that will capture a whole life, or make this loss feel smaller. But we can remember him together, and in doing so, remind one another that his life mattered deeply.

Jason was my brother, but he was also a friend, a colleague, and a member of this community. Each of us knew a different part of him. The stories you carry, the conversations you remember, and the ways he touched your life are all part of his legacy. I hope you will share them with one another—not only today, but in the days ahead.

Grief can come in waves. We may feel sadness, disbelief, gratitude, or even laughter when a memory comes back to us. There is room for all of it. We do not have to hurry through our sorrow or carry it alone. Being here together is one way we can help each other bear it.

Jason’s life does not end in this moment of farewell. It continues in the memories we keep, in the care we show one another, and in the ways his presence changed our lives. For me, he will always be my brother. I will miss him, and I will be grateful for him.

Thank you, Jason, for being part of our lives. We love you, we remember you, and we will carry you with us.
